_about: Complete release history, structured for the planned in-plugin 'What's New' viewer. CHANGELOG.md stays the human-readable copy; this file is the machine-readable one. Keep both in step when cutting a release. Newest release first. 'change.type' is one of: new, changed, fixed, removed, internal. 'published' is false for versions that exist in the repo's history but were never served from repo.json, so a viewer can skip them or fold them into the release that shipped their features.

releases.headline: Listing rosters, a party list that works on your own, and progression that stays put

changes.title: The listing panel shows who is in the party
changes.body: The panel beside a party finder listing now lists who is already in that party. One person in the party running the plugin is enough to describe the whole of it, so a listing is legible even when nobody else in it uses this. Only a publicly listed party is ever published, it is withdrawn when the listing ends, and the setting is under Settings -> PF Radar.

changes.title: Your own row while recruiting alone
changes.body: A listing posted with nobody in it yet now shows you, with your progression and a way to fetch it. The party list previously drew nothing at all until the first person joined, which is the one moment the information was worth having.

changes.title: Progression no longer disappears
changes.body: Prog points would drop back to "Fetch" while the server held the answer, most often with a listing open beside your own party list. The two panels shared one store and overwrote each other's results; each fight and character now has its own entry, so every surface shows the same answer at the same time.

changes.title: Update progress no longer swallows a press
changes.body: A press landing while the plugin was already reading was refused in silence, leaving a button that looked broken. Reads no longer block each other, and a press that genuinely cannot go through now says so.

changes.title: Omitted slots stay omitted
changes.body: Omitting a slot held until the first person left the party, at which point the locked-slot adjuster read every closed seat as a free one and recruited for the roles you had struck off. Closed seats are now left alone.

changes.title: Omitted slots are posted where the game puts them
changes.body: Omitted slots are now moved to the end of the listing before it is posted, which is the shape the game settles a listing into anyway. The roles you kept keep their order and slide up into the gaps.

changes.title: The "Read the update" button
changes.body: Removed from Settings -> About, along with the post it opened.

releases.headline: Two layouts, an overhauled UI, and duty spoiler locking

changes.title: Portrait and landscape layouts
changes.body: The window now comes in two fixed shapes: portrait, one column with a tab bar along the bottom, and landscape, wider with a sidebar and two-column pages. Neither can be resized - each is drawn for the size it is. Pick one in Settings under Appearance.

changes.title: Overhauled UI across the plugin
changes.body: New fonts, resized icons and buttons, and rounded corners throughout. Every prompt is now drawn inside the window rather than as a second window beside it, and confirmations are small centred alerts rather than full-width panels.

changes.title: Spoiler setting for unlocked duties
changes.body: A setting in Party Finder hides and locks any duty the current character has not unlocked, and stops such a preset being applied. Leave it off to see the duty names with locked ones marked, or turn it on to keep unseen content out of the picker entirely.

changes.title: Role slots default to a real composition
changes.body: With auto-select jobs off, slots used to be left free-for-all. Every category now has a default: a light party is a tank, a healer and two of anything that does damage, and an eight-player duty is two of each and four damage. A preset also carries only as many seats as its content fields.

changes.title: Clears notify on each new clear
changes.body: The Clears tab marks itself when somebody posts a clear you have not seen. Hearts are locked to the character that cast them and can be taken back by pressing again.

changes.title: The PF Analysis button steps aside
changes.body: It hides while the game's own recruitment criteria window or a listing's details are open, so the plugin is not offering a second button over a window that has already asked you something.

changes.title: FATEs and The Hunt stay on your world
changes.body: Both force "limit recruiting to my world" on, because neither survives the trip from another world, and your previous setting is restored when you pick a different category.

changes.title: Some duty categories are unavailable for now
changes.body: Duty Roulette, PvP, Gold Saucer, FATEs, Treasure Hunt and Deep Dungeons cannot currently be posted with the correct duty, so they are hidden rather than putting up a listing that says the wrong thing. Presets for them are kept and will return with the category.

changes.title: Presets saved without pressing Save
changes.body: Opening New preset created and saved the preset immediately. It is now only kept when Save is pressed.

changes.title: Dungeons were sized as a full party
changes.body: Light-party content now recruits four seats rather than eight.

changes.title: Omit did not omit the slot
changes.body: Omitting a role in the job selector had no effect while auto-adjust roles was on, which was the default for a new preset. Auto-adjust is now offered only where the game supports it, and the slot editor is yours everywhere else.

changes.title: Language letters were not centred
changes.body: J, E, D and F sat against the left edge of their buttons.

releases.headline: Downvoting fixed; ratings on by default

changes.title: Downvoting always failed with 'That rating couldn't be sent'
changes.body: A score validation check that was meant to block invalid values was also rejecting -1, the value a downvote sends. Upvoting was unaffected. The check now correctly accepts +1 and -1 only.

changes.title: Community ratings on by default for new installs
changes.body: The rating system master switch, the post-duty prompt, and ratings on the party panel all default to enabled. Existing installs keep whatever they had set.

changes.title: Apply was available while queued or in a duty
changes.body: The Apply button stayed green while you were sitting in the Duty Finder queue, and posting a listing from there drops your queue registration. It is now disabled - with the reason on hover - for the Duty Finder queue (including a popped duty awaiting acceptance) and while inside a duty.

changes.title: Presets half-applied from the World or Private tab
changes.body: The Party Finder remembers which of its three search-area tabs (Data Centre, World, Private) was last used, but recruitment can only be set up from Data Centre. Starting from either of the others broke the setup sequence partway. Applying a preset now forces the tab back to Data Centre first, whether or not the window is already open.

changes.title: Auto-Adjust Roles is on by default for new presets
changes.body: Mirrors the in-game 'Seek Job Distributions' option. It is what most listings want and it fills around whoever is already in your party. Only newly created presets are affected - saved presets keep whatever they were set to, since the field has always been serialised.

releases.headline: Preset sharing, macro support, and a refresher you can actually tune
releases.notes: Ships the 3.0.0 features as well - 3.0.0 was never served from the plugin repo, so users upgrade straight from 2.1.2 to this.

changes.title: Share presets with a one-line code
changes.body: Pick Share on any preset's menu and you get a single line of text with a copy button - paste it in Discord and anyone running PF Presets can use your setup. The Import button next to Create New Preset takes one back in, either pasted into the box or pulled straight off your clipboard. Codes that aren't PF Presets codes, or that got cut off mid-copy, are rejected with a plain explanation instead of importing something broken.

changes.title: /pfp apply <name>
changes.body: Posts a preset without opening the window, so a preset can live on a hotbar macro. Partial names work as long as they're unambiguous. Added /pfp list to see the exact names.

changes.title: Auto Refresher is no longer locked to 15 or 30 minutes
changes.body: Double-click the interval to type any value from 1 to 55. Next to it there's a new Stop after limit - set it and the refresher stops renewing your listing after that many hours, so a Party Finder can't sit up all night unattended. Your listing isn't cancelled when the limit hits; it just expires the way it normally would. 'Never' (the default) keeps the old behaviour.

changes.title: A renamed duty could post the wrong listing
changes.body: Presets recorded their duty by name and, when that name no longer matched, silently fell back to the first duty in the category - so a patch that renamed your duty could put up a listing for something else entirely. Presets now store the duty's id, which patches don't change, and when a duty genuinely can't be identified the listing is left with no duty set instead of guessing. Existing presets are upgraded automatically on first load.

changes.title: The window header shows the plugin version
changes.body: The line under the title now reads the running version instead of the preset count.

changes.title: Config schema v1
changes.body: Configuration.Migrate back-fills duty row ids for presets saved by earlier versions. Preset share codes are versioned behind a PFP1 magic prefix so the format can change later without breaking old codes silently.

releases.headline: Auto-adjusting locked job slots
releases.notes: Developed but never served from repo.json - its features reached users as part of 3.0.0.1.

changes.title: Auto-adjust locked job slots
changes.body: A toggle under the Auto Refresher. While you're recruiting as party leader, if a member leaves, any Party Finder slot locked to a single job is automatically widened to that job's role five seconds later - White Mage becomes regen healers, Red Mage becomes casters, Viper becomes melee - so the freed seat is easier to fill. If a slot is somehow locked to a non-combat job, it falls back to the standard auto-fill composition instead.

changes.title: A serious crash when duplicating or reordering presets
changes.body: Duplicating or reordering a preset from a card's menu could crash the plugin and, worse, corrupt the interface of Dalamud and every other plugin. Rendering is now hardened so a plugin error can never leak its styling into others.

changes.title: Taller preset cards
changes.body: Long descriptions are fully visible instead of being cut off.

changes.title: Ko-fi support button
changes.body: Added to the Applying Preset window next to the close button; the header button now reads 'Support me on Ko-Fi' with the heart.

releases.headline: Safety fixes and a delete confirmation

changes.title: Confirmation prompt before deleting a preset
changes.body: A misclick no longer wipes a preset instantly.

changes.title: A rare crash on unload mid-apply
changes.body: Could happen if the plugin was unloaded or updated while it was in the middle of applying a preset.

changes.title: Safer duty selection
changes.body: If a high-end duty has been renamed or removed by a game patch, the plugin leaves the listing's duty unset instead of posting a wrong one.

changes.title: Two options that never did anything
changes.body: 'Unselect Classes' and the item-level 'or Above' toggle were saved but never applied to the Party Finder.

changes.title: Codebase reorganised into Data / Game / UI
changes.body: No change to saved presets.

releases.headline: The Auto Refresher works end to end

changes.title: Auto Refresher performs the full Edit to Apply Changes sequence
changes.body: Matching the RecruitmentRefresher plugin's approach, so your Party Finder is reliably re-posted instead of just opening the window.

changes.title: Live countdown timer
changes.body: Sits next to the Auto Refresher toggle and shows the time until the next refresh. It starts once your Party Finder is up.

changes.title: Choice of refresh interval
changes.body: Every 15 or 30 minutes.

changes.title: /pfp refresh command
changes.body: Refreshes your listing on demand.

releases.headline: Party detection fixes and a redesigned status window

changes.title: Party job detection works when members are in different zones
changes.body: Auto-adjust slots read party jobs from the social party list instead of the in-zone party list, so a teammate being on another map no longer wipes out their detected job.

changes.title: Party leader detection updates when lead is passed to you
changes.body: The plugin could still think you weren't the leader after leadership was handed to you, blocking recruitment. It now reads the live party leader at the moment you apply a preset.

changes.title: The built-in Auto Refresher actually works
changes.body: Refreshes every 30 minutes using the same proven method as the RecruitmentRefresher plugin. The toggle sits as its own section above the Create button instead of overlapping it.

changes.title: Redesigned the Applying Preset window
changes.body: Matches the modern look of the rest of the plugin, with a friendly play-by-play and a smooth progress bar. Finishing shows 'All set, PF is up!' and a green Done button. The old settings-comparison list was removed.

changes.title: Assorted UI fixes
changes.body: Moved the Ko-fi button into the window header and made it bigger, surfaced the Auto Refresher toggle in the main window (hidden automatically if you have RecruitmentRefresher), fixed the Create New Preset button icon, and fixed long preset comments so they wrap instead of running under the Apply Preset button.

releases.headline: Private-party password moved out from behind the Apply button

changes.title: Password shown next to the preset name
changes.body: It's no longer hidden behind the Apply Preset button.

changes.title: Revamped design, usability and readability
changes.body: Reworked the look of the plugin throughout and fixed various bugs.

releases.headline: Applying a preset selects the right duty

changes.title: Presets no longer post as 'All'
changes.body: Applying a preset would often leave your listing set to All instead of the duty you saved, and you had to manually open the in-game duty menu once before presets would work. Applying a preset now sets the correct duty on its own.

releases.headline: Initial releases
releases.notes: Covers 1.0.5 and earlier; individual release dates were not recorded.

changes.title: Party Finder preset manager
changes.body: Save and manage Party Finder recruitment presets - duty, objective, roles, conditions, languages and more - and apply them with one click.
